html:
The Larrakia are the Aboriginal people of the Darwin area in the Northern Territory, around Port Darwin and the Cox Peninsula. They call themselves Saltwater People, and their life was built around the sea, the mangroves and the harbour.

They traded, held ceremonies and married with neighbours such as the Tiwi across the strait, the Djerimanga to the east and the Wadjiginy to the south. Makassan fishers from Sulawesi visited this coast in the 1700s and 1800s.

In 1869 the South Australian government founded the town of Palmerston, later Darwin, on Larrakia land. The Overland Telegraph Line reached it in 1872, and the town grew fast while the Larrakia were pushed to its edges. In 1972 Larrakia people sent a petition with more than a thousand signatures asking the Queen for land rights, the Larrakia Petition. Their claim to land around Darwin went on for decades. For the wider story, see Aboriginal Australian societies.
